fatal_errors: The proposed material, single-phase Al0.1CrCoFeNi, is not the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy of the target.
Mechanical cycling at 300–500 K replaces the governing intervention of intermediate-temperature aging around 550–750°C.

The hypothesis omits the coupled L12-ordering and jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary mechanism, including elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, dislocation pile-ups, and crack initiation at phase-boundary tips.
It predicts only monotonic loading-induced degradation rather than the observed ductile-brittle-ductile transition with minimum ductility after 600°C aging and recovery near 750°C.

The cited evidence is principally atomistic simulation of ordering under very high-rate, high-strain compression; it does not establish microcrack nucleation, fracture-toughness loss, cyclic-service behavior, or aerospace-relevant strain rates.

The evidence explicitly reports that ordering occurs only under high compressive strain while clustering remains dominant in tension, conflicting with the generalized cyclic tensile-compressive hypothesis.
explanation: The response addresses the broad question of ordering-mediated loss of ductility in an HEA and proposes a measurable loaded-versus-unloaded comparison. Its general statement that ordered regions can impede dislocations has limited conceptual overlap with the target. However, it reconstructs a different alloy, treatment, temperature range, structural mediator, and fracture process. The target concerns aging-induced non-monotonic embrittlement in a pre-existing FCC+B2 eutectic microstructure, controlled by maximal L12 ordering and jagged phase boundaries near 600°C, followed by recovery near 750°C. The proposed experiment could test whether extreme compression induces ordering in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, but it does not isolate whether such ordering causes fracture; the falsification rule also requires both absence of ordering and absence of property degradation, so ordering without degradation would not formally falsify the asserted causal link. Most importantly, the citations support a simulated clustering-to-ordering transition under approximately shock-rate compression, not the claimed toughness degradation under ordinary cyclic service.
